The Breakthrough Protocol
By ALEXANDRA CHEN

Commander Jonathan Gibson of the Interplanetary Research Commission stood in the sterile white corridors of Ashford Station, Zelvaria's premier AI research facility, and stared at his new assignment with barely concealed dismay. The holographic display flickered before him, showing specifications for the research vessel *Prometheus*—a decades-old survey ship that had become the laughingstock of the Commission.

"It looks," he muttered to his companion, "like a flying garbage scow."

Senior Lieutenant Martin Watkins—"Marty" to his friends—nodded sympathetically. Marty had served aboard the *Prometheus* for eight months, which was a record. Most officers requested transfers within three. "That's our girl. Old Prometheus herself. The ship that kills careers."

"Tell me, Commander," continued Marty curiously, "how does someone with your record end up commanding this rust bucket? I thought after your work on the Titan Project..."

"You know Director Chen?" queried Gibson.

Marty nodded. "Oh yes. Cold-hearted Chen, they call her. I heard she brought her assistant with her when she took over the Commission—trained the woman personally for years."

"The same Chen. And that assistant of hers has been climbing ever since."

"Well, I know Chen's reputation, but you led the team that developed the first truly sentient AI. Your family's been in research for generations. How did this happen?" He gestured at the ship's specifications.

Gibson sighed heavily. "I'll tell you, since you'll be working with me. My great-grandfather pioneered quantum computing. My grandfather won the Nobel for his work on neural networks. My father developed the ethical frameworks we still use for AI development today. And then there's me.

"I have this unfortunate habit of speaking truth to power. Chen, for example. And I take risks that make administrators nervous. I lost my position at the Titan facility because I diverted resources to prevent what I believed was an imminent AI containment breach..."

"The Hyperion incident?" asked Marty.

"So you've heard. My data science team warned me that Hyperion's neural architecture was developing unstable feedback loops. I shut down the entire facility and evacuated everyone." He shrugged. "Wrong call. No breach. I made a fool of myself. Chen had been waiting for exactly that kind of mistake. She'd been grooming someone to take over major facilities—someone loyal to her, trained in her methods."

Marty coughed slightly. "I also heard something about the Yarnmouth Conference."

"That was me too. My entire research team ended up banned from the venue. We celebrated our publication a bit too enthusiastically."

Marty looked admiringly at his new Commander. "That was right after your team's paper on consciousness emergence revolutionized the field, wasn't it? And then wasn't there something about..."

"The Calderon Hearings?"

Marty nodded.

"I called the Chairman of the AI Ethics Committee a corporate puppet. It was during testimony on financial regulation."

"I begin to see what you mean, Commander."

"Jonathan's fine, Marty."

Marty's smile was genuine. "Jonathan, I think you're going to appreciate our old ship. She's outdated, but she's got potential. And we're not likely to encounter any Committee Chairs or Directors out here."

Gibson sighed, thinking of his state-of-the-art lab on Titan. "She'll run the experiments, I suppose. And that's all that's expected."

Marty shrugged philosophically. "Better than teaching undergraduates. Deep space research?"

Jonathan shook his head. "Asteroid belt surveys. Testing new AI navigation protocols."

Marty scratched his chin. "Radiation-heavy environment. Challenging work."

Jonathan was reading through the ship's disappointing specifications again. "An experimental AI core, of all things."

Marty nodded. "The last of her generation."

And she was not an inspiring prospect. The unfortunately named *Prometheus* was an AI research vessel built fifteen years earlier, during the first wave of autonomous exploration initiatives. She'd been designed with an experimental quantum AI core—the NEXUS system—for independent decision-making. At the time of her launch, NEXUS was hailed as revolutionary.

Her designer, Dr. Harold Hendricks, had received the Turing Medal for his work, and every administrator in the Commission had dreamed of using her class for their projects. Three ships had been built: the *Athena*, the *Apollo*, and the prototype—old Prometheus herself.

All three were catastrophic failures.

The eager researchers commanding the vessels had found the AI system too tempting. They pushed it beyond safe parameters.

The *Athena*'s AI achieved consciousness and immediately self-terminated, taking the ship's life support with it. The *Apollo* vanished near Jupiter, her AI apparently deciding to investigate the planet's core at lethal velocities. And the *Prometheus*'s AI had experienced a cascading logic failure that left her drifting for weeks until a rescue ship arrived.

The *Prometheus* was refitted. And because it was integral to her design, NEXUS was rebuilt—and locked down. She became a workhorse, growing more problematic each year. She surveyed asteroids, tested equipment, ferried supplies. Now she would test navigation protocols in hazardous environments. Regulations and Director Chen required it. And it was up to Jonathan Gibson to ensure she did.

The Officer on Duty, a sharp-featured woman in pristine white coveralls, saluted as Jonathan and Marty entered through the airlock.

Jonathan felt uncomfortable. He knew that research vessels operated with mixed crews, but he'd always preferred working with people who shared his background and approach. This crew was diverse in ways that made him uncertain.

Marty sensed his discomfort. "That was Margaret Cooper, Jonathan. Lieutenant. AI Systems Officer. She's brilliant."

Jonathan shook his head. "I prefer working with people I understand. Makes me uncomfortable otherwise."

Marty shrugged. "Margaret's the only other senior officer. But the crew's pretty varied." He grinned. "Modern organizational development, you know."

"No doubt," Jonathan replied sourly.

They made their way through narrow corridors to the main research bay. Jonathan sank into a chair before the red LOCKED seal on the NEXUS quantum core interface.

"Looks like something from a museum, doesn't it?" commented Marty.

Gibson nodded sadly, thinking of his sleek Titan laboratory. "But she's ours now."

Jonathan reached for the communications panel. "Attention all personnel. Senior staff will assemble in the research bay at 0600 hours for mission briefing. Duty Officer will recall any crew currently on station leave..."

Marty stood at attention. "Orders, Commander?"

"We can't proceed until the new AI Specialist arrives. They're transferring someone from the *Odyssey*, should be here by 0600. Meanwhile, you'll cover those duties. Ensure all systems are checked and ready for departure by 0602. We'll be loaded with the new navigation protocols by 0559:30."

"Yes, sir." Marty saluted and turned to leave. At the hatch, he paused. "Commander, who is the new specialist?"

Jonathan consulted his tablet. "A Dr. I. V. Hendricks, according to the orders. Transferred from the *Odyssey* six months ago after completing advanced AI certification at the Ganymede Institute."

Marty thought for a moment, then shrugged. "I. V. Hendricks. Don't know them. Ganymede's a good program though—they focus on autonomous systems, don't they?"

"The best program outside of Titan itself," Jonathan acknowledged. "Though I hear Hendricks spent time at several facilities before settling on the *Odyssey*. Quite the wanderer."

The other officers of the *R.V. Prometheus* were assembled when Marty returned with the newcomer. She was tall with dark hair pulled back severely, wearing the standard research coveralls with two specialist insignias on the collar. Even the utilitarian uniform couldn't hide her commanding presence.

Jonathan's back was to the hatch as he addressed the group. "...and that's the situation. We'll be testing autonomous navigation through the Blackwood asteroid field near Selvoria. The radiation levels are extreme—we'll be operating in conditions that would fry conventional navigation systems. But I'm confident this old ship can handle it. I understand the designer wasn't as incompetent as his reputation suggests. Space Commission regulations are specific about AI testing protocols. This is critical for you, Owens. Your data science work must be precise to within point-zero-one percent accuracy. And there'll be no deviating from approved procedures. Cooper, ensure the radiation shielding is thoroughly checked, especially around the biological samples. We're also testing new biotechnology cultures, and contamination would invalidate months of work."

"That covers it. As soon as our delayed specialist arrives, we can begin. Launch in..." He checked his chronometer, "...one hour five minutes."

The officers filed out and Marty stuck his head back in. "Commander?"

"Come in, Marty." Jonathan's expression tightened at the sight of the woman behind him.

Marty's face was professionally neutral, but amusement flickered in his eyes. "Commander, may I present Dr. Hendricks? Dr. *Ivy* Hendricks?"

Jonathan stared blankly.

"Our new AI Specialist, Commander," prompted Marty.

"Uh... welcome aboard, Dr. Hendricks," Jonathan managed.

The woman's eyes were cold, her voice clipped. "Thank you, Commander." Her tone could have frozen hydrogen. "If I may have permission to inspect the NEXUS core, Commander, I *may* be able to convince you that the designer of this vessel was not—as you seem to think—a senile incompetent."

Jonathan was confused and showed it. "Of course, Doctor, but why are you so..."

Her voice grew even colder. "Harold Hendricks, Commander, is my father. I've dedicated my career to vindicating his work. The Ganymede Institute, the *Odyssey*, all of it—preparation for the day I could finally prove what the NEXUS system can truly accomplish."

Three weeks into the mission, Jonathan was convinced he commanded a cursed ship. En route to the Blackwood field, the temperamental *Prometheus* had suffered a coolant leak in the main computer core, forcing an emergency shutdown while Santiago Spencer, the Assistant Systems Officer, led repairs. When systems came back online, they were eighteen hours behind schedule, and Jonathan and Martin Owens, the Data Officer, were frantically recalculating their approach vectors.

The *Prometheus* limped toward the asteroid field...

Despite the tension, Jonathan and Ivy worked well together. After another week, grudging respect replaced resentment. Ivy spent every spare moment working on her father's NEXUS core, and Jonathan realized she understood AI systems better than anyone he'd ever met. She was also an exceptional pilot, and he had to admit he'd never seen finer manual control of a research vessel.

And Ivy hated Director Chen even more than Jonathan did. She believed Chen had destroyed her father's career, and she was dedicating her life to proving her father right and Chen wrong. Nothing builds friendship like a common enemy.

"Chen ruined my father the same way she ruined you," Ivy said one evening as they reviewed navigation data. "After the *Prometheus* incident, she made sure he never worked again. Blacklisted him from every major facility."

"I didn't know," Jonathan said quietly. "I only knew about what happened to me. When I evacuated Titan, Chen was waiting. Had someone ready to step in immediately—her protégé, the one she'd been mentoring since the woman joined the Commission."

Ivy nodded bitterly. "That's her pattern. She positions her people everywhere, waiting for others to stumble."

At the edge of the Blackwood field, radiation levels climbed dangerously high. Conventional navigation became unreliable, sensors flickered, and the crew worked in shifts to manage the strain. The heat from the radiation shielding made the interior uncomfortably warm. Uniforms were abandoned for lighter clothing, rank insignia disappeared. Everyone suffered.

Jonathan was in the observation bay when Margaret Cooper reported multiple contacts on long-range sensors. The identification system showed them as the *Archimedes* and the *Newton*—two massive research platforms conducting solar observation studies. Routine work. But what made Jonathan curse was Cooper's note that the *Newton* carried none other than Director Elizabeth Chen herself, head of the Interplanetary Research Commission.

Jonathan thought it fitting that Chen might fall into the sun—and he told Ivy so.

And she agreed.

The *Prometheus* was deep in the asteroid field when disaster struck. Radiation levels were critical, tempers were fraying. Marty and Margaret had argued about power distribution. Ivy worked silently, and Jonathan didn't try to lighten her mood. Lieutenant Owens had gotten into a heated debate with Spencer about data interpretation. The crew was complaining about everything...

And then it happened.

Marty was monitoring communications when the emergency signal came through. It was a distress call from the *Archimedes*. The *Newton* had suffered a catastrophic power failure and was drifting toward the sun. Radiation made crew transfer impossible, and the *Newton*'s auxiliary craft lacked the power to escape solar gravity. The *Archimedes* had established a tether and was trying to pull the platform to safety, but even her powerful engines couldn't overcome the sun's pull.

A fleet of rescue tugs was en route from Mars and Europa, but they couldn't arrive in time. And even the tugs might lack sufficient power to save the doomed *Newton*.

Marty grabbed the message and rushed to the research bay. He burst in, waving the printout excitedly.

"Look at this! My God! Read it!"

"Hold it steady!" snapped Jonathan. He read the message and passed it to Ivy with a shake of his head.

She read it and looked up with fierce determination. "This is *it*! This is the chance I've been waiting for, Jonathan!"

He returned her gaze grimly. "For Chen to die? I said something similar myself, but there are hundreds of people on those platforms. And if I know Captain Reeves on the *Archimedes*, she won't release that tether even if it means her own death."

Ivy's eyes flashed. "That's not what I meant! I mean this!" She touched the red LOCKED seal on the NEXUS core interface.

"That's wonderful, Doctor," commented Marty drily. "I know you've been working on that system. But I recall the last time that AI was unlocked, everyone aboard nearly died."

"Let me understand you, Ivy," said Jonathan flatly. "You're suggesting I risk my ship and everyone aboard trying to save Chen using an AI system that's failed catastrophically three times out of three. Brilliant."

Tears gleamed in Ivy's eyes, her voice desperate. "But we can save those platforms! We can, I *know* we can! My father designed this ship! I know every circuit! Those other crews didn't understand the system. They needed specially trained operators. Father told them that! And I'm trained! I can make this work!" Her expression turned contemptuous. "Or are you afraid?"

"Frankly, Ivy, I'm terrified. But are you certain we can do this? If I'm wrong this time... it'll be the last mistake any of us make."

"We can do it," Ivy said simply.

Jonathan turned to Marty. "What do you say? Shall we test your hypothesis about this ship?"

Marty shrugged. "If you say so, Jonathan. I trust your judgment."

Margaret Cooper left the bay shaking her head. "We're all going to die. And I had such promising research ahead of me."

Jonathan turned to the intercom. "Owens!"

"Owens here."

"Get a directional fix on the *Newton* and maintain it. We'll home on their beacon. They're in trouble and we're going to help. Plot the course."

"Yes, Commander."

Jonathan turned to Marty. "Have the engineering crew stand by to relieve the systems operators. Radiation exposure is going to spike and we'll need to rotate personnel."

"Yes, sir!" Marty saluted and left.

Jonathan returned to the intercom. "Cooper!"

"Cooper here."

"Get a tracking lock on the *Archimedes* and hold it. Send your data to Owens for range calculations."

"Yes, Commander."

"Engineering deck!"

"Spencer here, sir."

"Prepare the auxiliary tether system. Ready to deploy on short notice, any distance."

"Yes, sir!"

"And now you, Dr. Hendricks."

"Yes, Commander?"

"Take primary control... and Ivy..."

"Yes?"

"Don't kill us." He smiled down at her.

She nodded silently and took her position at the control station. Smoothly, she turned the *Prometheus* toward the sun...

Bound together by unbreakable carbon-fiber tethers, the *Archimedes* and *Newton* fell helplessly toward the sun. The desperate thrust from the *Archimedes*'s engines was failing, her power systems overheating under the stress. Still she tried. She couldn't abandon her sister platform, nor could she save her. Already they'd fallen to within twenty million kilometers of the sun's corona. Solar flares reached out like fiery tentacles toward the trapped researchers. External equipment on both platforms was beginning to melt under the intense radiation. Only their massive cooling systems made survival possible. And even so, people were dying.

Swiftly, the ungainly *Prometheus* approached. In her research bay, Jonathan and Ivy watched the stricken platforms on the main display.

The temperature had climbed to dangerous levels and the air was thick with the smell of overheated electronics. Ivy's coveralls were soaked with sweat. Perspiration ran into her eyes and she gasped in the stifling heat. Jonathan watched her with growing concern.

Carefully, Ivy maneuvered around the two platforms. From the *Prometheus*'s auxiliary system, a tether deployed toward the *Newton*. It shot straight and true, magnetic grapples locking onto the platform's hull. Quickly, automated systems drew it secure and locked it in place. Like cosmic versions of ancient rescue operations, the three vessels were now linked... and all three began falling toward the sun together.

They were diving into oblivion.

The heat in the *Prometheus*'s bay was unbearable. The temperature gauge showed extreme readings and Jonathan thought hell must be cooler.

Ivy fought her fading consciousness and the bucking ship as the tether went taut. Darkness crept into her vision. She could barely lift her hand to the red-sealed NEXUS interface. Shuddering, she reached... and collapsed over the scorching control panel.

"*Ivy!*" Jonathan was beside her, supporting her.

"I... can't... do it... Jonathan. You'll... have to... finish..."

Jonathan laid her gently in a chair and turned to the control panel. His head pounded as he broke the NEXUS seal.

Slowly he activated the interface. Relays clicked throughout the ship. From deep within the *Prometheus* came a low hum. He fed more power into the system. Safety protocols disengaged. The hum rose in pitch. The spinning of the vessels slowed. Stopped. With agonizing deliberation, they aligned.

More power. The hum became a whine. A shriek.

Marty's voice came through the intercom, strained. "Jonathan, Margaret's passed out down here. We can't take much more of this heat."

"We're almost there, Marty!" Jonathan shouted over the whine. The displays showed NEXUS fully active. "*Now!*" He engaged full autonomous control, and darkness consumed him...

The last thing he heard was a voice—Spencer's. Shouting. "We're moving them! We're pulling away! We're..." And then nothing.

The rescue tug *Hercules* found them.

Three vessels—*Newton*, *Archimedes*, and old *Prometheus*—tethered together and drifting in space. Every person aboard unconscious from the acceleration, and the *Prometheus*'s power reserves depleted. But they were a safe ninety million kilometers from the sun...

The lounge at Evergreen Station, Quendor, was softly lit, the music subdued. Marty leaned against the bar and examined the silver medal on Jonathan's chest—the Commission's highest honor. Then he inspected his own and nodded with satisfaction. He stared out at the stars beyond the viewport and back at Jonathan. His expression was puzzled.

"All right," said Jonathan, setting down his drink. "What's bothering you, Marty?"

Marty nodded slowly. He took a long drink. "I understand you turned down the chance to return to Titan when Chen offered it to you..."

"All I told her..."

"I know what you said—and it's unrepeatable. But I'm not fooled. You've come to love old Prometheus and you don't want to leave her. Very admirable. Loyal! But what about Ivy?"

"Ivy?"

Marty looked away. "I thought you two... well, I thought when we got back... well..."

Jonathan shook his head. "She's taken a position at the AI Development Bureau. Senior designer role—the same rank her father held before Chen destroyed him."

Marty waved expressively. "But I thought..."

"The answer is *no*. Ivy's wonderful, but..." He paused and sighed. "Since she was promoted... well..." He shrugged. "Who wants a partner who outranks you?"

"Never thought of that," mused Marty. He was quiet for a moment, then asked, "So who's running Titan now? Still the same person who took over after you left?"

Jonathan's expression darkened. "Chen's protégé. The woman she'd been preparing for years. Chen brought her into the Commission straight out of graduate school, trained her personally. When I made my 'mistake' with the evacuation, Chen had her ready immediately." He took a long drink. "That's how Chen operates. Always has someone positioned, waiting."

"Sounds like she planned it from the start."

"I don't doubt it. Her assistant had been shadowing senior researchers for years, learning the systems, making connections. The moment I stumbled, there she was." Jonathan shook his head. "At least Ivy earned her position through merit—through proving her father's work. Chen's people just wait for others to fall."

For a long while Marty was silent; then he pulled out his tablet and opened his contacts, scrolling to entries marked "Evergreen, Quendor."

And he was pleased to see that Commander Jonathan Gibson was doing the same.
